=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Positions

**Scope:** This review is based on the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter, not the full SPA text, so clause-level drafting still needs checking. It is an AI-assisted analysis for the Wattlebridge deal team and should be confirmed by Australian (NSW) transaction, tax, and privacy counsel before it is used in negotiations.

**Headline:** The four known items (Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 0.42m, Ironquay AUD 0.18m, Sandbar AUD 0.33m) total about AUD 4.13m, roughly 86% of the Seller's proposed AUD 4.8m general cap. Bluefen adds about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue at risk. These are known, quantified exposures and should be handled through price adjustments, conditions precedent, and specific indemnities, not left to general warranty claims.

| ID | Issue | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| N-001 | General cap | Counter |
| N-002 | De minimis & basket | Counter |
| N-003 | General time limit | Counter |
| N-004 | Fundamental/title regime | Reject |
| N-005 | Fraud carve-out | Require |
| N-006 | Disclosure scope | Reject |
| N-007 | Buyer knowledge | Reject |
| N-008 | Bluefen consent | Require |
| N-009 | Riverlark facility | Require |
| N-010 | Employee bonuses | Require |
| N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | Reject / Counter |
| N-012 | Export/privacy incident | Require |
| N-013 | Sandbar renewals | Counter |
| N-014 | Category separation | Require |
| N-015 | Title verification | Require |
| N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | Reject |

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller position:** General warranty claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer should want:** A higher general cap, around 30–50% of price (AUD 7.2–12m), given the known issues. Fundamental and tax claims sit under separate caps (see N-004, N-014).
- **Recommendation: Counter.** The cap is the main ceiling on recovery, and the known items would consume most of AUD 4.8m.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller position:** AUD 25k de minimis. AUD 250k basket, deductible (only the excess is recoverable).
- **Buyer should want:** A lower de minimis (around AUD 10k), related claims aggregated, and a tipping basket so that once exceeded, recovery is from the first dollar. Fundamental claims and specific indemnities excluded.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** The AUD 250k amount (about 1% of price) is within a normal range, but a deductible structure means the Buyer absorbs the first loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller position:** Claims notified within 18 months of Completion, and the limitation applies to all claims.
- **Buyer should want:** 24–36 months for general warranties, so the Buyer covers at least one full year-end cycle. Tax claims run to the ATO amendment period plus a buffer. Fundamental claims run longer (see N-004).
- **Recommendation: Counter.** 18 months is too short for a business whose FY26 accounts and tax positions will not be fully tested in that window.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority) capped at 100% of price, outside basket and de minimis, with a 6-year claims period (or the statutory period).
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Title is the foundation of the deal, and administrative convenience is not a reason to cap it like general warranties.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** Not addressed in the package. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," which would catch fraud.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out so nothing in the limitation, exclusive remedy or non-reliance provisions limits claims for fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller. These claims should be uncapped and not subject to the general time limit.
- **Recommendation: Require.** Courts generally read limitation clauses narrowly, but an express carve-out removes doubt and the "any nature" wording must be narrowed.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012, as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026), the accounts, statutory registers and public searches, "without limiting" specific disclosures.
- **Buyer should want:** General data room disclosure deleted. Disclosure only against specific warranties, against a fair disclosure standard, and by specifically identified document. Disclosure should never cut down specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** General disclosure of the whole data room would effectively eliminate the warranty protection.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller position (cl 8.3):** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Clause deleted and replaced with a pro-sandbagging clause: the Buyer's knowledge does not affect its rights to claim. Known risks should be dealt with through specific indemnities or price, not by excluding claims.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The Seller would be using the Buyer's own diligence to shift the risks it warranted, and this would combine with N-006 to remove most protection.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller position:** The Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. No final consent is in the data room, and clause 11.3 conditions are unmet. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer should want:** A final written Bluefen consent, with clause 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion (waivable only by the Buyer). A Seller obligation to procure, not endeavours. "Delivery" defined precisely. If consent is not obtained, a deferred payment or escrow, or a specific indemnity for revenue loss.
- **Recommendation: Require.** About 30% of revenue is at risk, so this is a condition precedent, not a reasonable-endeavours matter.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller position:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding. Release to be provided after Completion. No discharge of security is in the data room. Change-control clause 8.1 is referenced.
- **Buyer should want:** On a debt-free basis, repayment at Completion from the price, using a payout letter. Discharge of security (including PPSR releases and guarantees) delivered at Completion. Riverlark change-of-control consent confirmed if cl 8.1 requires it.
- **Recommendation: Require.** A debt-free deal requires repayment and release at Completion, not after it, or the Buyer funds the debt and is exposed to the security.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller position:** Conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420k. Not in the draft funds flow. Described as "a matter for the Seller." Payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs not addressed.
- **Buyer should want:** Treated as a debt-like item and deducted from price, or paid by the Seller before Completion. Payroll tax, super and on-costs quantified and allocated to the Seller. Post-Completion vesting conditions dealt with expressly. Seller indemnity for all bonus-related liabilities.
- **Recommendation: Require.** Under a debt-free/cash-free basis, AUD 420k of Completion-triggered liabilities cannot sit outside the funds flow.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, described as adequate. Clause 7.3 transfer of SOW3 materials is conditional on cleared payment. AUD 180k is open. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** Before Completion, evidence that all SOW3 fees are paid, or the AUD 180k deducted from price. A confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay of all SOW3 project materials. An indemnity covering any Ironquay claim about IP ownership, title, third-party claims or unpaid fees, surviving beyond the general time limit and outside the general cap.
- **Recommendation: Reject / Counter.** IP title and payment must be fixed before Completion, and an indemnity limited to one SOW payment does not cover the risk.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller position:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material. DL 6 records a download link sent to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) may be exposed. Access and notification obligations are unresolved. No loss amount stated.
- **Buyer should want:** A forensic investigation and a Privacy Act assessment before signing. Business contact details can still be personal information. Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, the company must assess a suspected eligible data breach promptly (within 30 days). If the company was aware before late September, that window may already have passed, so this needs urgent confirmation. Also: a specific indemnity for regulator, notification, remediation and third-party costs, uncapped or under a separate cap; a Seller pre-Completion conduct covenant; and possibly an escrow.
- **Recommendation: Require.** "Not expected to be material" is unsupported by any loss analysis, and the Buyer should not inherit regulatory exposure without a specific indemnity.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller position:** Three renewals at AUD 110k each (AUD 330k aggregate), described as ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Confirmation of the period each renewal covers. Pre-Completion amounts borne by the Seller or treated in working capital. Post-Completion amounts borne by the Buyer. Termination rights and any change-of-control terms reviewed. Confirmation that the renewals were not split to fall below thresholds (DL 8 says to read them together).
- **Recommendation: Counter.** "Ordinary course" does not allocate cost under a debt-free/cash-free basis, so the timing split must be agreed.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** A single regime. All claims subject to the same caps and time limits.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regimes for: (i) general warranties (cap, basket, 24–36 months); (ii) fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority) capped at price, 6 years; (iii) tax warranties and a pre-Completion tax indemnity, capped at price, to the ATO period plus buffer; (iv) specific indemnities (Bluefen, Ironquay, privacy, Riverlark, bonuses) outside basket and de minimis; (v) fraud unlimited. Known debt-like items handled through price adjustment, not claims.
- **Recommendation: Require.** A single regime would leave the known risks inside the AUD 4.8m cap.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller position:** Title shown by the company share register at DD-012 (Harbourglass 100%). The Buyer has not yet verified.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification before signing: ASIC company extract, the company's own register of members, share certificates, a PPSR search over the shares, confirmation of no options, convertible rights or other share issues, and directors' resolutions approving the transfer. Title warranties sit in the fundamental regime (N-004) and transfer documents executed at Completion.
- **Recommendation: Require.** A seller-prepared register is a source document, not a verification, and the Buyer should complete its own searches before signing.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties described as "settled under the general regime." The Seller's own summary treats them as open.
- **Buyer should want:** Tax warranties and a pre-Completion tax indemnity, capped at price, with a time limit tied to the ATO amendment period plus a buffer. IP warranties (ownership, non-infringement, Ironquay-related) treated as fundamental or separate, with a longer time limit. Payroll tax from the bonuses (N-010) covered.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** These are not settled; they need separate negotiation and cannot sit under the general cap.

---

### Other items outside the list
- **Office lease (DL 7):** Check the lease for change-of-control or assignment provisions. Obtain landlord consent or confirmation if required, and consider a landlord estoppel as a condition precedent.
- **Mossvale (DL 9):** Confirm the assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. Get written confirmation, or consent if the clause captures a change of control, as a condition precedent.
